title: No source gives the field-level shapes this story needs: the change-report element beyond its legacy field names, the CSV column order, the rulesChanged element, the decision-code and item-list values, the reconciliation read and the DP-02 login name
source: Legacy RWB-E2-041 sections 7, 8, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 17 against FSD P7 v3 A2.7 and A2.8, TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1, the Ownership Map rule-package and decision-log rows, and Architecture v5 slides 13, 14 and 41
description: The legacy story fixes the facts of the report and none of the shapes. It names the RulePackageChangeEntry fields but not their nesting, not the CSV column order and not where the rows added, changed and removed of BR6 sit; it names rulesChanged[] without an element shape. It writes the decision code and the final call of a governance entry as literals of its mapping, and no LOV table carried in the extract lists the values of LOV-DECISION or a final-call list, so both are read as reference data whose values and list codes are not given. The reconciliation of AC10 is 'the total matches GET /api/recovery/v1/decision-log for the same period and package version', but the decision-log read of TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 (API-P7-006 and API-P7-007) filters by case, decision, rule, approver and date range and has no package-version filter, so the equal-count assertion has no operation to name and this story reads decision_log_entry in service instead. Neither the checklist item-list code nor the answer of the load and the approve with the legacy flag off is written out, and the per-service database login of DP-02 is named nowhere.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-041 section 7 AC1 to AC10, section 8 BR6 and BR8, section 10 (the Rules and parameters right R and the roles RW-COE, RW-RISK, RW-AUDIT, RW-PLATADM), section 11 (DF-REF-274 to DF-REF-297 and DF-DEC-004, DF-DEC-005), section 12 (the change-report table with its query and its RulePackageChangeEntry field list, and 'No events are published'), section 13 (the three indexes ix_rpv_loaded_at, ix_rpv_approved_at and ix_rpv_valid_from), section 14 (MSG-P3-022, MSG-GEN-003, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P7-002, MSG-P4-002); FSD P7 v3 A2.7 AC-P7-007-01 and A2.8; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031), T3.2 (LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-PRODUCT and no LOV-DECISION) and T-A.1 (API-P7-006, API-P7-007); Architecture v5 slide 13 (P7 calls P4 by REST, listens to nothing, writes files) and slide 41 (one schema and one login per service)
proposed: Agree the shapes at the wave 2 contract review of RWB-P3-E2041-CON and of this service: the ChangeReportPage and RulePackageChangeEntry with the rulesChanged element as ruleId, added, changed and removed, the CSV column order equal to the JSON field order, the decision code of a governance entry and the checklist item-list code in LOV-DECISION and its sibling list, the package-version count read on decision_log_entry, the answers of the load and the approve with the legacy flag off, and the name of the rwb-decision login. Until then the story builds and tests against ASM-B2-P7-006-1, ASM-B2-P7-006-5 and ASM-B2-P7-006-6 and the fakes of section 12.8.

title: The metadata rows name no build dependency and the P3 contract only, while the DP table adds eight platform contracts and four published contracts, and the registry operations this story amends sit in another lane of the same service
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP table rows DP-01, DP-03, DP-04, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-11, DP-13, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 against the plan story record of RWB-P7-E2041-APP, the fragments of RWB-P7-E2042-APP and RWB-P3-E2041-CON, and Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41
description: The story record carries Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P3-E2041-CON. The twelve patterns the story applies add eight platform contracts and four published contracts the metadata does not carry: DP-03 H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-04 H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, DP-06 H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-07 H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-08 H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON, DP-14 H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, DP-15 H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and DP-19 H RWB-PLT-N001-CON; DP-01, DP-05, DP-11 and DP-13 add none. The legacy story also depends on RWB-E1-073 (the load, the approve and the rollback of a package version) and RWB-E1-037 (the permission matrix), which in the target are RWB-P7-E2042-APP in lane L-P7-AO and RWB-P4-E1037-CON. RWB-P7-E2042-APP is the same service but a different lane: this story adds one part to its load and four checks to its approve, so a worker cannot tell from the plan whether this story waits for it or builds against its published operations.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-01, DP-03, DP-04, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-11, DP-13, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 and R5.7 rules 1 to 3; the story record of RWB-P7-E2041-APP (H [], C ['RWB-P3-E2041-CON']); legacy RWB-E2-041 section 3 (RWB-E1-073, RWB-E1-037) and section 10; the fragment of RWB-P7-E2042-APP (H [], C ['RWB-P3-E2042-CON'], lane L-P7-AO) and of RWB-P3-E2041-CON (the six consumed operations of this service); sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13 of this story
proposed: Read the H list of the story as None plus the eight platform contracts the DP table names, and the C list as RWB-P3-E2041-CON plus C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON; treat RWB-P7-E2042-APP as the published registry operation set this story extends, which an APP story builds against with the fake of section 12.8, and keep Ready to start at Day 1. Re-check at the wave 2 kick-off that the registry operations are published.

title: The legacy story places the change checklist and the report in module P3 and the P4 package recovery.accessadmin.rulepackages with a P3 feature flag, while the target puts the registry, the checklist column and the decision log in rwb-decision
source: Legacy RWB-E2-041 sections 1, 3, 12, 13, 15 and 18 against Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings, R4, the Ownership Map rows of P7 and P4, and Architecture v5 slides 4, 13 and 14
description: The legacy story is filed under module P3 Case and workflow, places the endpoint and the version writes in the P4 package recovery.accessadmin.rulepackages, names the feature flag rwb.p3.rule-change-report, and puts the report beside SCR-39 of the administration screens; its checklist column DF-REF-295 lives on rule_package_version. In the target the rule package registry is P7 rwb-decision by the R3 default ruling and the Ownership Map, and the table rule_package_version is P7's; the screens stay with P4 and the case-side read with P3. The ownership of the checklist, the approval checks and the report is therefore split by table and not by the legacy module pointer, and the legacy flag keeps a P3 prefix under a P7 owner.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-041 metadata (Module P3 Case and workflow), section 3 (the feature flag rwb.p3.rule-change-report), section 12 (the endpoint and the P4 published interface of RulePackageVersionService), section 13 (the package recovery.casewf.rules.audit and recovery.accessadmin.rulepackages), section 15 (no screen in this story, SCR-39 in Epic 8) and section 18; Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings (rule package registry to P7 rwb-decision; parameters and reference data to P3; feature flags to the platform library) and R4 (schema and login per service); Ownership Map rule package and decision log rows of P7; the fragments of RWB-P3-E2041-APP, RWB-P4-E2041-APP and RWB-ITG-E2041-ITG
proposed: Keep the split the plan makes: rwb-decision owns the checklist column, the two amended operations and the change report because it owns rule_package_version and decision_log_entry; rwb-case owns the case-side audit read and the impact count; rwb-access owns the screens and the rights. Keep the legacy flag name as a legacy reference read as a parameter of rwb-decision, and record the rename in the run Change Register rather than editing the legacy story.

title: Legacy AC1 approves ALLOCATION version ALLOC-2026.12 on 2026-12-02 while AC5 loads the same version on 2026-12-08 and approves it on 2026-12-09, so BR4 (verify on or after the load and before the approval) cannot hold in both readings
source: Legacy RWB-E2-041 section 7 AC1 and AC5 against its section 8 BR4 and its section 4 steps 2 to 5
description: AC1 loads ALLOC-2026.12 with request CR-2026-0042 from 2026-12-10 and has it approved by U-51 on 2026-12-02, and its Then asserts the approval time is before the valid-from date. AC5 loads the same version label on 2026-12-08 with verify note and verify date 2026-12-08 and approves it on 2026-12-09, and its Then asserts that the checklist holds the verify date, the load time and the checksum 9f2c...e1b4. BR4 requires the verify item to be dated on or after the load and before the approval. Read together, the same version is approved five days before it is loaded, and a verify date of 2026-12-08 would fall after an approval of 2026-12-02. No source reconciles the two runs.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-041 section 7 AC1 ('U-51 approves version ALLOC-2026.12 on 2026-12-02', 'valid from 2026-12-10') and AC5 ('loaded on 2026-12-08 with verify note ... and verify date 2026-12-08', 'U-51 approves it on 2026-12-09'); section 8 BR4 ('The verify item is dated on or after the load and before the approval'); section 4 steps 2 to 5 (load, store, approve) and section 5 X5 (a verify date before the load is refused with MSG-GEN-003)
proposed: Read AC5 as the run this story tests — load 2026-12-08, verify date 2026-12-08, approval 2026-12-09, valid from 2026-12-10 — because it is the only reading that satisfies BR4 and X5, and leave the 2026-12-02 approval of AC1 with RWB-P3-E2041-APP, which owns that criterion. Confirm with the business analyst before SIT whether the legacy intent was two separate ALLOCATION versions.
